definitions.explanation: An extreme reaction of surprise or shock at something unexpected. Stronger than ordinary surprise, implying the person is so startled they metaphorically look up at the sky.

examples.japanese: その{知|し}らせに{仰天|ぎょうてん}した。
examples.english: I was astounded by the news.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{発言|はつげん}に{周|まわ}りの{人|ひと}は{仰天|ぎょうてん}した。
examples.english: The people around him were astounded by his remark.

examples.japanese: {値段|ねだん}を{聞|き}いて{仰天|ぎょうてん}するほど{高|たか}かった。
examples.english: The price was so high that I was shocked when I heard it.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a noun or with する to express extreme surprise or shock. The word literally means "looking up at the sky" ({仰|あお}ぐ + {天|てん}), evoking the image of someone so startled they throw their head back. Often appears in the pattern {仰天|ぎょうてん}する or ～に{仰天|ぎょうてん}する.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仰天|ぎょうてん}する (to be astounded)
- {仰天|ぎょうてん}ニュース (shocking news)
- ～に{仰天|ぎょうてん}する (to be astounded at ~)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {驚|おどろ}く: to be surprised — more general and milder
- びっくりする: to be startled — more colloquial
- {唖然|あぜん}とする: to be dumbfounded — emphasizes speechlessness
